items.followUp: Define the moment of a force and state the SI unit of moment.

rubric.why: Identifies what the moment of a force describes.
rubric.description: Defines moment as the turning effect of a force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that moment is the turning effect of a force about a pivot or point. Accept equivalent wording that describes its tendency to rotate an object.

rubric.why: States the relationship used to calculate moment.
rubric.description: Gives the product of force and perpendicular distance from the pivot to the force’s line of action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct product and perpendicular distance.

modelAnswer: The moment of a force is its turning effect about a pivot or point.
Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force.

items.followUp: A force of 8 N acts perpendicular to a spanner 0.25 m from its pivot. Find its moment.

rubric.why: Recognises that gravitational attraction is mutual.
rubric.description: States that you and the Earth attract each other.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that both exert an attractive force on one another.

rubric.why: Applies Newton’s third law to compare the forces.
rubric.description: States that neither force is larger; they are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the forces are equal in magnitude (and opposite in direction).

modelAnswer: You attract the Earth, and the Earth attracts you.
Neither exerts a larger force: the forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

items.followUp: What is the value of the acceleration due to gravity on the Moon?

rubric.description: Defines g as the acceleration due to gravity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying g as the acceleration produced by gravity (near the Earth’s surface).

rubric.why: Checks the standard approximate value and unit.
rubric.description: Gives g ≈ 9.8 m/s² (often rounded to 10 m/s²).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct approximate value with acceleration units.

modelAnswer: g is the acceleration due to gravity.
Near the Earth’s surface, g ≈ 9.8 m/s² (approximately 10 m/s²).

items.followUp: A machine receives 500 J of energy and produces 350 J of useful work. Calculate its efficiency.

rubric.why: Identifies the ratio that defines efficiency.
rubric.description: Defines efficiency as useful output divided by total input.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct useful-output-to-total-input ratio.
Award 1 mark for the correct mathematical formula, including multiplication by 100 for percentage efficiency.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output work (or energy) to total input work (or energy).
Efficiency = (useful output ÷ total input) × 100%.

items.followUp: A motor produces 45 J of useful work from 300 J of input energy. Find its efficiency.

rubric.why: Checks the correct ratio of useful work to input energy.
rubric.description: Substitutes the useful work and input energy into the efficiency ratio.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using 12 J ÷ 100 J (or an equivalent ratio of 0.12).
Award 1 mark for the correct efficiency with percent unit.

modelAnswer: Useful work = 12 J; input energy = 100 J.
Efficiency = (useful work ÷ input energy) × 100%.

items.followUp: State Newton’s second law of motion and use it to obtain F = ma for a body of constant mass.

rubric.why: Checks the law’s statement in terms of momentum.
rubric.description: States that the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the rate-of-change-of-momentum statement.

rubric.why: Includes the direction specified by the law.
rubric.description: States that the change in momentum occurs in the direction of the applied force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction.

rubric.why: Establishes the momentum relation needed for the explanation.
rubric.description: Uses momentum p = mv for a body of constant mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct momentum expression in the explanation.

rubric.why: Checks the standard mathematical form derived for constant mass.
rubric.description: Obtains Newton’s second-law equation F = ma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final equation.

modelAnswer: Newton’s second law states that the rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction of that force.
Momentum, p = mv.
For a body of constant mass, rate of change of momentum = (mv − mu) ÷ t = m(v − u) ÷ t = ma.
Therefore, F ∝ ma; in SI units, F = ma.

items.followUp: A vehicle starts from rest and travels 600 m in 60 s with uniform acceleration. Find its speed at the end of 60 s.

rubric.why: Checks the given quantities and conversion to SI units.
rubric.description: Identifies u = 0, s = 1 km = 1000 m, and t = 100 s.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly recording the initial speed, distance in metres, and time.

rubric.why: Checks use of the uniform-acceleration equation and calculation of acceleration.
rubric.description: Uses s = ut + ½at² to find a = 0.2 m/s².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the appropriate equation and 1 mark for a correct substitution/calculation of acceleration.

rubric.why: Checks the final speed calculation, including its unit.
rubric.description: Uses v = u + at to obtain the final speed, 20 m/s.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final-velocity equation/substitution and 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: u = 0 m/s, s = 1 km = 1000 m, t = 100 s.
Using s = ut + ½at²: 1000 m = (0 m/s)(100 s) + ½a(100 s)².
Using v = u + at: v = 0 m/s + (0.2 m/s²)(100 s).
The speed at the end of 100 s is 20 m/s.

items.followUp: Estimate how many seconds are in 14 years. Use 365 days per year.

rubric.why: Checks that a reasonable age estimate is stated.
rubric.description: Assumes an age of about 15 years for the estimate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating a reasonable assumed age; accept a different clearly stated age if the conversion is carried out consistently.

rubric.why: Checks the conversion from years to seconds and the estimated result.
rubric.description: Converts the assumed 15 years to approximately 4.73 × 10⁸ s.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct seconds estimate consistent with the stated age.

modelAnswer: Assume my age is about 15 years.
